paragraphs.en: Scientific War lets you choose each card instead of always playing the next one. Win all the opponents' cards, using special powers to change a contest or prepare an advantage for the next.
Two to eight players begin with equal sets of ranks: 2 through ace and one joker each. Suits do not affect strength.
Everyone chooses privately. Browse your hand with the arrows and submit a card with Enter. T tells you who has chosen; the cards are revealed once all players are ready.
Each group of played cards is a trick. The highest card normally wins them all. Ranks rise from 2 through the number cards, then jack, queen, king and ace. V reads the last trick's result.

Your winnings wait separately from your hand. Only after playing every card in your current hand do you pick up the captured cards to use again. Having neither a hand nor captured cards eliminates you.
A tie for the strongest card begins a war: nobody collects the pile, and all players still in the game choose another card. The next outright winner takes that trick and the earlier unclaimed cards.
Further ties keep building the pile until someone wins it alone.
These cards act when played, even if they do not win:

- A jack reverses rank strength in the very trick where it is played. A 2 becomes strongest and an ace weakest, until a later reversal. Jacks in the same trick cancel in pairs: two leave the order unchanged, three reverse it once.

- A queen lets you choose last on the next trick, after seeing the opponents' cards. Wait for their choices, press C to read them, then choose yours with the arrows and Enter. Two or more queens in one trick give nobody this privilege.
- A 3 lets C read opponents' hand sizes on the next trick. Ordinary E reads total card counts, including captured piles.

- An 8 offers a hand swap on the next trick. Press C before choosing a card to exchange your whole hand with your captured pile, or keep the hand you have. You need at least one captured card to swap.
R reads whether high or low cards currently win and which power you can use.
A joker changes the result according to the other cards:
- If the other cards would tie for strongest, a single joker breaks the war and its player takes everything.
- If the other cards would produce one winner, a single joker denies that win and starts a war. The pile stays for the next trick.
- Two or more jokers cancel their effect, leaving the other cards to decide.
You win when nobody else has cards. If a war exhausts everyone's cards and nobody can finish it, the game is a draw.
Play also ends after 50 tricks. Count both hands and captured piles; the largest combined count wins, with equal largest counts drawing.
The host can set a different limit from 20 to 100 tricks. Card counts decide the result at that limit in the same way.
Arrows: choose a card.
Enter: play the selected card.
Z: select the next card, or play it if it is your only card.
Shift+Z: select the previous card, or play it if it is your only card.
C: use your power: inspect choices after a queen, hand sizes after a 3, or swap hand and pile after an 8.
E: read total card counts.
T: read who has chosen.
R: read rank order and available powers.
V: read the last trick's result.
